author: reek
body: Direction is the only attenuation axis the capability model has, and until now the compiler threw it away: manifest-cap-bytes wrote a literal readwrite for every capability it emitted, and boot-cap-mask-for did not look at direction at all. So a program declaring [FileSystem.Read] was granted filesystem READ AND WRITE at boot, and put a READWRITE capability into its own manifest for any verifier that read it. The loader's dir-bits honoured read-only grants correctly the whole time -- it was simply being told the wrong thing.

author: reek
body: Console is declared bare, so it asks for both directions and must get them -- an attenuation that also denies what was legitimately asked for is not attenuation, it is a bug. Reporting the console bits proves the derivation does not simply clear every write bit it sees.

author: reek
body: The bits are read through process-get-cap, which is what the kernel itself tests before it services a syscall. This is the granted word, not a restatement of the source.
